reconstructed_theorem_text: Let E be a complete finite-dimensional real inner product space with its Borel measurable structure, μ a probability measure on E, and C a positive real number. Suppose that for every smooth compactly supported real-valued v on E, the integral of v² log(v²) minus the integral of v² times the logarithm of that integral is at most 2C times the integral of the squared norm of the gradient of v, with all integrals taken against μ. If a pair (f,w) in scalar and E-valued L²(μ), respectively, belongs to the joint norm closure of the pairs represented μ-almost everywhere by (g,∇g) for smooth compactly supported real-valued g on E, then the variance of f under μ is at most C times the squared L²(μ) norm of w.
objects: The space E, probability measure μ, positive constant C, smooth compactly supported tests v and g, their Riesz gradients, and an L² pair (f,w).
domains: v and g map E to ℝ; their gradients map E to E; f lies in L²(μ;ℝ) and w in L²(μ;E), both taken modulo μ-almost-everywhere equality.
quantifiers: For every admissible E, μ and C, if the test inequality holds for every smooth compactly supported v, the conclusion holds for every pair (f,w) in the specified closure. Each generating pair has a single existential witness g for both coordinates.
assumptions: E is complete and finite-dimensional over ℝ with an inner product and its Borel measurable structure, μ is a probability measure, C > 0, the logarithmic inequality holds on the test class, and the pair belongs to the stated closure.
scopes: Smoothness and compact support are global. The logarithmic hypothesis concerns smooth tests only; log(0) is taken as 0. Pair membership uses joint norm closure, with both generating equalities understood μ-almost everywhere. No single-valued gradient on arbitrary L² classes is assumed.
constant_dependencies: The same fixed C appears as 2C in the test inequality and C in the variance bound, uniformly over all eligible tests and pairs for the fixed E and μ.
